questions.prompt: Which graph shows y = 2x/(x² - 4), with its asymptotes dashed?
questions.prompt_markup: Which graph shows y = 2x/(x² - 4), with its asymptotes dashed?
questions.grading_note: Zero and y-intercept 0; vertical asymptotes x = ±2 (zeros of x² - 4); horizontal asymptote y = 0 (degree of numerator < degree of denominator); e.g. y(3) = 6/5 > 0 and y(1) = -2/3 < 0. The others show 2x/(x² + 4), 2x²/(x² - 4), and the reflection.

figure.description: Four graphs labeled A to D, each on a grid with x from -6 to 6 and y from -5 to 5. Graph A: one smooth curve with no vertical asymptotes, through the origin, with a high point at (2, 0.5) and a low point at (-2, -0.5). Graph B: three branches separated by dashed vertical asymptotes x = -2 and x = 2; horizontal asymptote y = 0; the middle branch falls through the origin; the left branch is below the x-axis and the right branch above it. Graph C: three branches separated by dashed vertical asymptotes x = -2 and x = 2, with a dashed horizontal asymptote y = 2; the middle branch touches the origin from below. Graph D: three branches separated by dashed vertical asymptotes x = -2 and x = 2; horizontal asymptote y = 0; the middle branch rises through the origin; the left branch is above the x-axis.
